summary: Score side of the quality phase, applying client feedback 2026-10-27 16:20 (items 1 and 2) and 16:45 (solo piano, arpeggios), plus the lead's two notes. (1) Velocities: every note event carries ScoreEvent.velocities (0..1, loudest of merged duplicates), and MIDI export uses them. (2) Sustain pedal: inferred from the raw notes as Score.pedals (absolute ticks; spans that touch are a pedal change). Evidence is 3 or more notes from 2 or more earlier onsets still ringing within 19 semitones; changes go at the onset whose notes outlive the joint release. Output: Ped. / * marks in ABC (abcjs 6.7 has no !ped!, so an invisible V:PED voice carries the annotations), MusicXML <pedal> with damper-pedal sound, MIDI CC64 on both hands. (3) Arpeggios no longer vanish: distinct onsets never share a tick (onset clusters in source time, isotonic fit to the 16th grid, crowded runs spread in order), so the polyphony cap only ever trims truly simultaneous chords. (4) Two voices per staff (Staff.voice2) where a sustained note (1.8x longer, or 1.3x louder under pedal) holds over two or more later onsets of its hand. The first voice keeps Staff.measures; ABC writes voices sharing a staff (%%score {(RH RH2) | (LH LH2 PED)}); MusicXML voices 1/2 and 5/6 with backup and stems. Bach's Prelude now shows the held tenor (dotted eighth tied to a quarter), and the real Liebestraum shows the cantabile C4 under the arpeggio as Liszt writes it. (5) Adaptive hands (splitMode 'auto'): a beam search over onsets. Hands follow the music: melody over a high accompaniment, arpeggios kept in one hand, crossing only against recent attacks, a velocity stream cost. splitMode 'fixed' is the manual override. (6) Per-staff clefs by ledger-line count (a high left hand gets V:LH clef=treble). (7) Tempo octave: candidates are scored on tracked beats, with notation terms for long upper-line notes and for a beat with no subdivision. The client's ballad case now reads 70 bpm, not 140-144. (8) Rubato: a dynamic-programming beat tracker with tempo continuity produces AnalysisResult.beatTimes when the map is not straight; buildScore maps seconds to ticks through it; sourceSecondsAt / tickAtSourceSeconds give 'Original' sync. (9) Pickup bars (AbcOptions.pickup; MusicXML implicit measure 0). (10) Harmonic spelling by line-of-fifths context: Ab in an Fm6/C chord in C major, augmented C-E-G# keeps G#; tie continuations keep their attack's letters. (11) Meter: short 3/4 excerpts (4-5 bars) are detected when the ternary pattern dominates. Results on audio-accuracy's 12 real fixtures (Salamander renders with pedal, rubato, room, phone/video/TikTok variants; ground-truth notes with pedal-lengthened durations used as an ideal transcription): tempo, meter, downbeat and key right in 11 of 12. Notes at their exact written tick: real-ballad 60/60 (was 9/60 at 140 bpm), real-liebestraum 74/78 (6/4 written as 3/4), real-elise 51/52, real-mozart 123/123, real-moonlight 35/35 grid notes (66 bpm; was 200), Gymnopédie 34/34 (now 3/4). Pedal precision 0.71-0.98 on fixtures with pedal; recall about 0.8. Synthetic sweeps: 0 tempo/meter/downbeat errors on 992 steady streams and on 24 rubato ballad/Liebestraum performances. | ROUND 3 (client feedback 19:55 and 21:15, real Liebestraum recording): measured the engine against the aligned reference (local only). Root cause of the 'horrible rhythm': beat tracking. With the reference beat map the same transcriptions reach rhythm accuracy 0.80/0.81 and halfbar downbeat F 0.97. With the engine's own beats they get 0.04/0.10, beat F 0.47/0.49, 4/4 instead of 3/4 for 6/4, and key A instead of C. The engine fails the same way on the reference notes themselves (beat F 0.52), so this is not transcription noise. The tempo swings 85-270 bpm. Tried and reverted (no gain): a tempogram tempo curve, a tatum curve and wider tracker windows. Even the TRUE tempo curve only reaches beat F 0.46, so the blocker is beat PHASE (on- vs off-beat eighths in a continuous eighth texture), not tempo. Triplets are not the issue here (4 of 1347 onsets). Done this round (client 21:15): notes are notated as played, not as the pedal sustains them. Under the pedal a note is cut at the next note of its hand, and no later than the next note of either hand or its beat end; held voices and clearly louder melody notes keep their length. Ties per note 0.38->0.28 (piano model), 0.41->0.35 (Basic Pitch); 0.29->0.20 with the oracle beats. Notated lengths within x1.5 of the reference: 0.49->0.53 (oracle 0.56->0.61). When the pedal covers 60 % or more of the score, ABC shows one 'con Ped.' instead of Ped./* pairs; Score.pedals, MIDI CC64 and MusicXML pedal are unchanged (playback keeps the sustain). Triplets / sextuplets NOT implemented (plan below); a synthetic sextuplet fixture exists and currently reads 91 bpm 3/4 (sextuplets as straight 16ths at 1.5x tempo).

public_api_notes:
Import everything from 'src/engine/score'.
VELOCITIES: ScoreEvent.velocities is on every note event (tied pieces repeat the attack's values), parallel to pitches, 0..1 rounded to 0.001; rests have none. Legacy scores without velocities: use DEFAULT_VELOCITY (0.7).
PLAYBACK: scoreNotes(score) returns PlayedNote[] {pitch, tick (absolute), ticks (ties merged), velocity, staff 0|1, voice 1|2}, sorted. It covers both staves and both voices. Seconds at the score tempo: tickToSeconds(score, tick).
PEDAL: Score.pedals?: PedalSpan[] in absolute ticks, sorted, non-overlapping, clipped to the score. A span ending exactly where the next starts is a pedal CHANGE: dampers fall and the pedal goes down again at that tick, so notes attacked there are held by the new span. Absent = no pedal detected. The pedal is inferred in every build (memoized per notes array and filter settings).
SECOND VOICE: (staff as VoicedStaff).voice2?: Measure[]. Same length as measures; each measure tiles [0, ticksPerMeasure); its rests are invisible. Staff.measures stays the FIRST voice with its old role: it tiles, matches the viewer's timeline, and its ABC line is still V:RH / V:LH = tune.lines[i].staff[s].voices[0]. The second voice is V:RH2 / V:LH2 = voices[1] on the same staff. staffVoices(staff) returns [measures] or [measures, voice2]. Voice 1 is the upper voice (stems up). tie: true continues into the next event of the SAME voice. A key struck again in the other voice cuts the sounding note.
CLEFS: Staff.clef may be 'treble' for the left hand (or 'bass' for the right) when that saves most ledger lines. ABC writes V:LH clef=..., MusicXML the matching clef.
HANDS: EngineParams = ScoreParams & { splitMode?: 'auto' | 'fixed' } (buildScore accepts it). defaultParams returns splitMode 'auto': hands follow the music and splitPoint is only a soft centre. 'fixed' or absent: pitch >= splitPoint goes right (old behaviour; stored docs and the demos). sanitizeParams keeps splitMode.
ABC: scoreToAbc options pedalMarks?: boolean (default false; drive it from Settings.sustainPedal) writes an invisible V:PED voice on the lowest shown staff with 'Ped.', '*' and '* Ped.' annotations (a blank line first when note names are on, so they stack under the names; %%annotationfont is emitted). pickup?: boolean (default false): measure 0 is written without its silent first beats (pickupTicks(score) ticks), so abcjs time and elements start that many ticks after Score tick 0. Spelling is harmonic: the sounding chord decides between sharp and flat.
MUSICXML: scoreToMusicXml(score, { pickup?: true }): implicit measure 0 when the music starts at least a beat late. Voices 1/2 (staff 1) and 5/6 (staff 2), <pedal type=start|stop line=no sign=yes/> with <sound damper-pedal/>.
MIDI: scoreToMidi uses the score velocities, both voices, CC64 (SUSTAIN_CC) value 127/0 at span edges on both tracks.
RUBATO / SYNC: analyzeNotes may return AnalysisResult.beatTimes (source seconds of each tracked beat) when the tempo is not straight (RMS deviation over 3 % of a beat, or any beat 10 % off). Then bpm is the median tracked tempo and beatOffset is a tracked beat. buildScore maps seconds to ticks through the map (scaled by params.bpm / analysis.bpm, so halving 'Tempo base' still works). For 'Original' playback use sourceSecondsAt(score, tick, analysis) and tickAtSourceSeconds(score, seconds, analysis). Without beatTimes they equal startSeconds + tickToSeconds.
OTHER: inferPedalSeconds(sourceNotes), createTimeMap, pickupTicks, MusicXmlOptions, PedalSeconds, PlayedNote, VoicedStaff, SplitMode, EngineParams.
TIMING (3 000 random notes, this machine, other agents running): buildScore median 3-10 ms over all difficulty and hand modes (min 2-8 ms); first build of new notes about 20 ms; scoreToAbc about 14 ms; analyzeNotes about 74 ms for a 190 s rubato piece (once per transcription).
ROUND 3: ScoreEvent durations under the pedal are now ARTICULATED (written as played). The sustain lives only in Score.pedals: renderers must apply Score.pedals for the ringing (piano-sound already does). New exports: pedalThroughout(score) and PEDAL_THROUGHOUT (0.6). With scoreToAbc({ pedalMarks: true }), a score that is mostly pedalled gets one 'con Ped.' annotation at the first pedal start; local pedalling still gets Ped./* per span. No TimeSignature or tick-model change.

requests.request: src/types.ts (additive): add ScoreParams.splitMode?: 'auto' | 'fixed' (absent = fixed) and Staff.voice2?: Measure[] with the doc comments of EngineParams (build.ts) and VoicedStaff (notes.ts). The engine already writes them at runtime and exports those types; once they are in types.ts, the viewer can drop its casts.

Make the split point a real manual override: onChange={(v) => patch({ splitPoint: v, splitMode: 'fixed' })}. Optionally show 'Auto' while params.splitMode === 'auto'. 'Restablecer' (initialParams/defaultParams) brings back 'auto'. Until then, moving the stepper only shifts the auto split's soft centre.

For the stored recording use sourceSecondsAt(score, tick, doc.analysis) and tickAtSourceSeconds(score, seconds, doc.analysis) instead of score.startSeconds + tickToSeconds(...). With a rubato beat map (analysis.beatTimes) the constant mapping drifts by up to several beats.

Optional: pass pickup: true to scoreToAbc for a real anacrusis bar. Then skip the timeline events of measure 0 that start before pickupTicks(score) when mapping abcjs elements, and subtract pickupTicks(score) from abcjs times. The second voice (voices[1] in abcjs, Staff.voice2 in the Score) is not highlighted by the current map; piano-sound's pianoPlan already plays it.
scoreNotes(score) from the engine gives the same notes as pianoPlan's own scoreNotes (both voices, ties merged, velocities). Either is fine. Pedal changes are touching spans (end === next start).

known_issues: A strong final ritardando (25 % slower over the last beats) can put the last bar one sixteenth late (seen in the synthetic Liebestraum texture; the real fixtures are fine). The tracker locks its last beat on an off-beat onset.

Hands: an accompaniment note and a melody note less than 3 semitones apart that start together stay in one hand (real-ballad: 53/60 notes in the edition's hands). A left-hand sweep up to C5 kept in one staff uses ledger lines: no mid-piece clef changes or cross-staff beaming yet (abcjs has no cross-staff beams).

Pedal: sparse textures where fingers could hold the notes (Gymnopédie bass + chord) get little pedal (recall 0.30, precision 0.96). Marks use the annotation font, not a Ped. glyph (abcjs 6.7 has none).
Very short excerpts (5 bars) remain hard: fast sparse melodies can read at half tempo and short waltzes may get 4/4 (old engine 64/496 errors on such streams, new 66/496; all 12-bar streams correct).

The 'builds 3 000 notes in under 30 ms' test passed in the final runs but is load-sensitive: with other agents' Chrome/audio jobs on this machine, medians under vitest's parallel workers reached 33-40 ms during development, against 3-10 ms isolated.

round4.summary: ROUND 4 (agent score-readability; client feedback 2026-10-28 08:50 and 2026-10-27 21:15: reduce the elongated notes everywhere). (1) Triplets finished: TICKS_PER_QUARTER 12 (a sixteenth = 3 ticks, a sixteenth triplet = 2); each quarter beat takes a straight or a triplet grid by onset fit; written as ABC (3:2:n / (6:4:n, MusicXML divisions 12 with <time-modification>, MIDI ppq/12. The slow sextuplet reading wins the tempo choice: sextupletBallad reads 60 bpm 4/4 Eb major with sixteenth sextuplets (test passes for 3 seeds; the it.todo is gone). Triplet detection is now tempo-aware (onsets must sit more than 30 ms off the sixteenth grid, and a triplet beat needs 3+ onsets): false triplet beats on the Liebestraum recording 15 -> 10 (piano model, own beats), 14 -> 4 with the reference notes. (2) Readable durations everywhere (new engrave.ts): each note is written up to the next note of its own voice; under the pedal, or when the hand's earlier notes ring on (an undetected pedal), a note that is not held also ends by the next onset of either hand or its beat end; every articulated note is ONE simple value (the longest that fits; a rest fills the rest), so nothing articulated is tied across a beat or a barline. Held only with evidence: the held voice of a two-voice staff (new skyline rule: a right-hand melody note at the top of a figure a minor third or more below it for 1.5 beats and 1.15x louder gets its own voice even under the pedal), a key that really sounds that long without pedal and without ringing neighbours, and the final chord. A hand cannot hold a key over a note more than a tenth away (the written note ends there). Held notes end on the beat when within a sixteenth of it. Playback keeps the sound: Score.pedals as before, plus EngineEvent.sounding / PlayedNote.sounding (ticks a key sounded without pedal), which pianoPlan now plays. (3) Beat phase: no change survived (see known_issues).

results.metric_notes: Local-only evaluation (deleted from the repo; copy in C:/Users/Marcos/AppData/Local/Temp/pauta/score-readability/tools/eval.test.ts.txt). ties/n = tied continuations per written note, all voices. dur1.5 = matched notes (pitch, +-100 ms through the score's own time map) whose written length in seconds is within x1.5 of the reference length (Liebestraum: Krueger MIDI durations; realistic: the fixtures' notated durations). pos = share of reference notes at their written position under the best constant (scale, offset), 1/12-beat bins. Not the round-3 definitions: HEAD is re-measured with the same code.

round4.public_api_notes: Ticks: TICKS_PER_QUARTER = 12 (SIXTEENTH = 3; sixteenth triplet = 2; TUPLET_VALUES). Every tick consumer goes through engine helpers (secondsPerTick, ticksPerMeasure, beatTicksOf, sourceSecondsAt / tickAtSourceSeconds); nothing persisted stores ticks (ScoreDoc keeps notes + params; loops are in measures). Written lengths are articulated everywhere: renderers must not read the written length as the sounding length. New: EngineEvent extends ScoreEvent { sounding?: number[] } (attack events only, ticks from the attack per pitch, present when the key sounded longer than written without pedal); PlayedNote.sounding?: number (from scoreNotes, only when > ticks). MIDI and MusicXML keep the written lengths (plus CC64 / pedal marks).

One line changed in src/features/viewer/pianoPlan.ts (playNotes: end = tick + max(ticks, sounding)) plus a test, so playback keeps legato and held notes that sound without a detected pedal now that the notation is articulated. Review or take it over.

known_issues: Target dur1.5 >= 0.75 NOT reached on Liebestraum: 0.55 piano / 0.46 Basic Pitch with the engine's beats (HEAD 0.59 / 0.53), 0.64 / 0.51 with the reference beats (HEAD 0.60 / 0.51). Among notes at the right position the rule reaches 0.71 (piano, reference beats). The one-value rule shortens off-beat notes to the beat, and with the wrong beat map many notes look off-beat. Allowing one tie into the beat gave 0.60 but 0.13 ties per note, so it was rejected (the client's priority is no ties). Even the reference notes with the reference beats cap near 0.74: performed eighths at 0.67-0.78 of a beat quantize to sixteenths.

Ties target met: Liebestraum 0.041 piano / 0.061 Basic Pitch (0.34 / 0.44 at HEAD by this count; round 3 reported 0.28 with another count). Realistic mean 0.099 piano; outliers: Gymnopedie (hands split a chord; the final chord tied over 3 bars) and real-moonlight with the piano model (tempo read at 200).

Beat phase (task 3): nothing survived. Phase evidence (bass, top-line length, velocity accents, Viterbi with a switch cost) picks the right phase on 100 % of the reference beats, so the evidence is sound; but the engine's beat PERIOD is wrong: in 10 s windows the reference tempo swings 50-231 bpm while the tracker stays at 136-154. Phase correction on the engine's beats: beat F 0.47 -> 0.47-0.49 (piano), 0.49 -> 0.51-0.55 (Basic Pitch); wider tracker windows (0.5-2x period), a lower global penalty and phase-weighted accents: best 0.57. Not shipped. Next step: a tracker that allows tempo-octave sections (meno mosso / a tempo) before the phase step.

Triplets on real recordings: 10 tuplet beats remain in 163 s of Liebestraum (piano model; the reference has about 2); fast triplets (>150 bpm) are kept only when clearly 30 ms off the sixteenth grid. phone-moonlight-125 stays skipped in quality.test.ts: reading Moonlight as triplets needs a tempo-choice term for steady triplet streams (real-moonlight with the piano model reads 200 bpm).

distinctSlots spreads crowding globally: one beat with more onsets than grid points (a sextuplet beat read straight) can shift the stream before it by one slot (seen while tuning; the sextuplet tests guard it).
